The Deepholds of Karak Dûm.name: The Deepholds of Karak Dûm
The Deepholds of Karak Dûm.note:
Dwarven clans in the mountains of the Eastern Isle under Thane-King Durgrim Ashbeard, miners and smiths whose iron and arms are the best in the known world. The Deepholds sell weapons to every side and trust no one.
Character: Gruff, proud and suspicious. Dwarves keep their word and expect others to keep theirs, despise haste and shoddy work, and remember every slight for a century. They will sell to anyone who pays in full, and help no one for free.
Economy: Steel, arms and armour, the best in the world, with gems and worked stone. The coming war has doubled its prices and its orders. It grows little food under the mountains and buys grain from Veyl and the elves. Coin: the anvil, a heavy gold coin (1 anvil = 10 crowns). Output about 120 crowns a head a year, 55.7 million crowns in all; farming 10%, crafts and mining 70%, trade and services 20%. Debt 0% of a year's output, budget +6% (surplus), growth 1.5% a year, prices rising 1% a year, 3% of hands idle. It grows 30% of the food and 95% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Glass Republic of Veyl.name: The Glass Republic of Veyl
The Glass Republic of Veyl.note:
A mercantile city-republic on the Eastern Isle's sheltered bay, famous for its glass and its banks, governed by the Glass Senate under First Magistrate Cassia Venn. Veyl trades with every power, lends to all of them and is trusted by none.
Character: Polished, calculating and studiously neutral. Veyl's envoys are courteous to everyone, record every promise and every debt, and smile most when they are least committed. Its neutrality is its shield, and everyone suspects it is for sale.
Economy: Glass, lenses, mirrors and crystal from its furnaces, and above all its banks, which lend to every crown and hold much of the world's debt. It imports almost all its food and fuel by sea, so a war that closes the sea lanes would starve it. Coin: the glass ducat, the most trusted coin in the world (1 ducat = 5 crowns). Output about 220 crowns a head a year, 118.8 million crowns in all; farming 10%, crafts and mining 40%, trade and services 50%. Debt 20% of a year's output, budget +4% (surplus), growth 2.5% a year, prices rising 2% a year, 7% of hands idle. It grows 35% of the food and 40% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Elderwood.name: The Elderwood
The Elderwood.note:
The last realm of the old elves, in the forests of the Eastern Isle, under the Lady Ithrael. Few and fading, the elves remember the wizard Malgrath's first war, and fear that his return is near.
Character: Serene, sorrowful and distant. The elves speak in memories, think in centuries and warn more than they act; they look on the younger peoples with pity, and on Malgrath with a fear they hide behind courtesy.
Economy: Forest gathering, healing herbs, fine timber and elven craftwork, worth a great deal in the human markets but sold rarely and only through Veyl and the dwarves under the Pact. Its people are few and fewer every century. Coin: no coin: gifts and barter among the elves; others reckon its trade in crowns. Output about 90 crowns a head a year, 17.3 million crowns in all; farming 50%, crafts and mining 20%, trade and services 30%. Debt 0% of a year's output, budget 0% (surplus), growth -1% a year, prices rising 0% a year, 0% of hands idle. It grows 100% of the food and 100% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

Thornwatch.name: Thornwatch
Thornwatch.note:
A frontier march on the Great Isle's north coast, facing the Northern Isle across a narrow strait, ruled by the hereditary Warden, Garrick Stonehand. Its walls and ships are all that stand between the southern kingdoms and the Iron Horde, and it resents that the others do not pay for them.
Character: Grim, battle-hardened and distrustful of the soft south. Thornwatchers speak bluntly, sleep armed and measure everyone by whether they would stand on the wall. They expect to be left alone when the orcs come, and say so often.
Economy: Fisheries, timber and bog iron. Almost everything else goes on the wall: it borrowed heavily to rebuild after the Grey Strand, the other kingdoms have not paid their share, and every raid burns another harvest. Coin: Aldermere's crowns, and the Warden's iron ward-notes, promises to pay after the war (1 ward-note = 0.6 crowns). Output about 35 crowns a head a year, 35 million crowns in all; farming 55%, crafts and mining 25%, trade and services 20%. Debt 45% of a year's output, budget -6% (deficit), growth -1% a year, prices rising 4% a year, 4% of hands idle. It grows 70% of the food and 90% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Iron Horde of Gor-Vathra.name: The Iron Horde of Gor-Vathra
The Iron Horde of Gor-Vathra.note:
The orc clans of the Northern Isle, bound in fear to the Blackspire, a tower in the northern peaks where the undying wizard Malgrath the Unbreathing has ruled for longer than anyone remembers. The clan chiefs serve him and each dreams of his fall. Its longships have been sighted off Thornwatch.
Character: Brutal and hungry, but not stupid: the clans are loud, proud and quick to violence, while Malgrath plans in decades, through raids, spies, dark rites and traitors cultivated in the human courts. He speaks rarely, coldly and with terrible patience; the chiefs speak in boasts and threats.
Economy: Herds, iron mines and the forges of the Spire, and plunder from every raid. The clans' hungry winters are fed by raiding; the Spire's war is fed by iron sold through Veyl's banks, against which it has borrowed. Everything goes to war. Coin: no coin of its own: tribute in iron bars, captives and plunder, reckoned in iron weights (1 weight = 0.5 crowns), and Veyl's gold for its iron. Output about 20 crowns a head a year, 29 million crowns in all; farming 40%, crafts and mining 35%, trade and services 25%. Debt 15% of a year's output, budget -3% (deficit), growth 2% a year, prices rising 8% a year, 3% of hands idle. It grows 55% of the food and 90% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Ashen Exiles.name: The Ashen Exiles
The Ashen Exiles.note:
A clan of orcs that broke with the wizard Malgrath and fled to the far north-western islet under its chief, Grukk Oathbreaker. Hunted by the Iron Horde and distrusted by the humans, they might yet be turned against their old master.
Character: Hard, wary and bitterly honest. The Exiles hate Malgrath more than they hate anyone, trust no one who has not bled beside them, and speak plainly of the Horde's secrets to anyone who offers them a place in the world.
Economy: Fishing, seals and seabirds on a frozen islet that cannot feed them all; a little smithing with the iron they carried away. They have nothing to sell but their swords and the Spire's secrets. Coin: no coin: barter, and Horde iron taken in the flight. Output about 10 crowns a head a year, 0.5 million crowns in all; farming 70%, crafts and mining 20%, trade and services 10%. Debt 0% of a year's output, budget -10% (deficit), growth -3% a year, prices rising 0% a year, 5% of hands idle. It grows 45% of the food and 60% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

Hollowcrown.name: Hollowcrown
Hollowcrown.note:
A mountain kingdom in the foothills of the Great Isle's central range, ruled by Queen Ysolde, who is also High Priestess of the Silver Flame. Hollowcrown holds the passes through the mountains and despises Sunvale's softness and Morrowgast's witchcraft alike.
Character: Stern, devout and stubborn mountain folk who see the world as a battle between faith and corruption. They are honest and brave allies but judge everyone, forgive slowly and suspect any magic that is not blessed by their priests.
Economy: Silver and iron mines, the tolls of the high passes, and pilgrims to the Silver Flame. Its stony valleys do not feed it: it buys grain from Aldermere and Sunvale. The Prelacy's tithes keep the crown's purse full and the people poor. Coin: the hallowed mark, struck from its own mountain silver (1 mark = 1.5 crowns). Output about 40 crowns a head a year, 41.7 million crowns in all; farming 55%, crafts and mining 30%, trade and services 15%. Debt 8% of a year's output, budget +1% (surplus), growth 0% a year, prices rising 1% a year, 5% of hands idle. It grows 60% of the food and 85% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

Sunvale.name: Sunvale
Sunvale.note:
A wealthy and decadent kingdom in the warm southern lowlands of the Great Isle, ruled by the young and pleasure-loving King Florian II while his ambitious ministers govern. Its eastern border runs against Morrowgast, which has begun to test it.
Character: Charming, vain and full of intrigue. Sunvale's court loves art, festivals, fine marriages and gossip, and fears having to fight above all; it would rather pay, flatter or marry its way out of danger, and its ministers plot against each other even as the border burns.
Economy: Wine, olive oil, fruit, silk and the luxuries of the south; the fairest farmland of the Great Isle. Its court spends far more than it raises on festivals, palaces and gifts, the Grand Minister has quietly borrowed against the harvests from Veyl, and the eastern raids have emptied the border villages. Coin: the golden sol (1 sol = 3 crowns). Output about 75 crowns a head a year, 300.8 million crowns in all; farming 60%, crafts and mining 10%, trade and services 30%. Debt 55% of a year's output, budget -5% (deficit), growth 0.5% a year, prices rising 5% a year, 10% of hands idle. It grows 110% of the food and 75% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Coven-Realm of Morrowgast.name: The Coven-Realm of Morrowgast
The Coven-Realm of Morrowgast.note:
A human realm on the Great Isle's south-eastern arm, ruled by the Hag-Queens, a circle of witches led by Mother Vesk. Generations of their blood-rites have changed its people: taller, scarred, feverish and craving battle. Morrowgast seeks to spread this Blessing, and is testing Sunvale's border.
Character: Proud of what they have become and contemptuous of the 'unblessed', the Morrowgasti speak of war as worship and of the Blessing as destiny. They are savage in battle and grow more so each generation; some of their own people, quietly, are horrified.
Economy: Poor, blight-scarred farmland, fens, and witch-herbs and reagents sold to smugglers. Hollowcrown's priests forbid all trade with it and the Order hunts its caravans, so it lives on what it grows and what its war-bands take from Sunvale's villages. Coin: the coven groat, base silver stamped with a crow (1 groat = 0.4 crowns). Output about 25 crowns a head a year, 29.9 million crowns in all; farming 65%, crafts and mining 15%, trade and services 20%. Debt 5% of a year's output, budget -8% (deficit), growth -2% a year, prices rising 6% a year, 2% of hands idle. It grows 70% of the food and 80% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Order of the Lantern.name: The Order of the Lantern
The Order of the Lantern.note:
A monastery-state of witch-hunting knights in the mountains of the Great Isle under Grand Master Aldous Cray, sworn to destroy Morrowgast's Hag-Queens and all unholy magic. A useful ally to the kingdoms, and a fanatical one.
Character: Fervent, disciplined and merciless toward what they call corruption. The knights of the Lantern speak in vows, trust no magic but their own blessed light, and would burn a village to cleanse it; the kingdoms value their swords and fear their zeal.
Economy: Alms, bequests and the tithes of its faithful, the work of its lay brothers' farms, and the ransoms of captured witches. Preparing the crusade is costing more than its donors give. Coin: Hollowcrown's hallowed marks and alms in every coin of the Great Isle. Output about 30 crowns a head a year, 2.1 million crowns in all; farming 40%, crafts and mining 10%, trade and services 50%. Debt 10% of a year's output, budget -10% (deficit), growth 0% a year, prices rising 2% a year, 0% of hands idle. It grows 50% of the food and 80% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

Aldermere.name: Aldermere
Aldermere.note:
The oldest kingdom of the Great Isle, ruled from the lake city of Aldermere by King Edric IV through a vast and ancient court. It sees itself as first among the human kingdoms and the natural arbiter of their quarrels, and it is calling a council of the kingdoms against the threats in the north and the south-east. Its battle-mages come from the Conclave of the Lake, which serves the crown by charter but follows its own counsel.
Character: Proud, slow and legalistic. Aldermere answers every question with a precedent, every crisis with a council and every insult with a formal protest. Its neighbours find it pompous and its decisions late, but its word, once given, is kept.
Economy: Wool, grain and lake fish, and the tolls of the Lake Road, which carries half the Great Isle's trade. It buys glass and credit from Veyl and steel from the Deepholds. War levies for the north and the cost of the Council strain a treasury already in debt to Veyl's banks. Coin: the silver crown (the reckoning coin of the Great Isle). Output about 55 crowns a head a year, 335.6 million crowns in all; farming 65%, crafts and mining 15%, trade and services 20%. Debt 25% of a year's output, budget -2% (deficit), growth 0.5% a year, prices rising 2% a year, 6% of hands idle. It grows 85% of the food and 80% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles.name: The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles
aliases: The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles
The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles.note:
Pirates and free sailors of the small southern islands under Captain-General Red Mara, raiding the shipping of every power and selling their swords to whichever kingdom pays most. Their crews take anyone, orcs and exiles included.
Character: Swaggering, irreverent and fiercely free. The Brotherhood laughs at crowns, keeps its own rough honour, and will fight for anyone's gold but bow to no one; it respects nerve and despises the righteous.
Economy: Plunder, prizes, ransoms and smuggling, sold in the markets of Red Harbour; some fishing and salt-panning. A good year is a rich one and a bad year means hunger, since the isles grow almost nothing. Coin: whatever it takes: mixed coin reckoned in 'pieces' (1 piece = 1 crown). Output about 60 crowns a head a year, 5.9 million crowns in all; farming 5%, crafts and mining 15%, trade and services 80%. Debt 0% of a year's output, budget +10% (surplus), growth 3% a year, prices rising 10% a year, 15% of hands idle. It grows 25% of the food and 50% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

Westmarch.name: Westmarch
Westmarch.note:
The rich western lowlands and their harbours, the breadbasket and the chief port of the Great Isle, ruled by a council of merchant princes under First Prince Marro Bellweather. Westmarch quarrels with Aldermere over the tolls on the lake road.
Character: Pragmatic, cheerful and money-minded. Westmarchers bargain over everything, prefer a good deal to a good fight and will lend gold to anyone who pays the interest. They hate war that closes the harbours more than they hate any enemy.
Economy: The richest harbours of the Great Isle: grain exports, shipbuilding, shipping and the merchant princes' banks. Brotherhood raids raise the cost of insuring every cargo, and the Lake Road tolls eat into its trade with the interior. Coin: the gilder (1 gilder = 1.2 crowns). Output about 80 crowns a head a year, 361.8 million crowns in all; farming 45%, crafts and mining 20%, trade and services 35%. Debt 10% of a year's output, budget +2% (surplus), growth 1.5% a year, prices rising 3% a year, 8% of hands idle. It grows 95% of the food and 70% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Free Clans of the Lakeshore.name: The Free Clans of the Lakeshore
aliases: The Free Clans of the Lakeshore
The Free Clans of the Lakeshore.note:
Proud, poor and independent clans of the fens and hills south of the great lake, ruled by a moot of clan-mothers under Wenna of the Reeds. Every kingdom wants them as a buffer; none has ever ruled them for long.
Character: Prickly, proud and fiercely free. The clans answer to no king, settle quarrels by moot, and take any offer of protection as an insult, though they will trade, hunt and fight for whoever treats them as equals.
Economy: Fishing, fowling and reed-cutting, now without the fens that fed them: the scattered clans live on what they can hunt in the hills and what they take back from Aldermere's new holdings. Coin: no coin of its own: barter in fish, fowl, reeds and furs. Output about 15 crowns a head a year, 2.1 million crowns in all; farming 80%, crafts and mining 5%, trade and services 15%. Debt 0% of a year's output, budget -15% (deficit), growth -10% a year, prices rising 0% a year, 20% of hands idle. It grows 40% of the food and 70% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

The Conclave of the Lake.name: The Conclave of the Lake
The Conclave of the Lake.note:
The oldest and most powerful school of wizards in the world, seated in the Tower of Stars on the isle of Wyn in Aldermere's great lake, under Archmagister Corvane Thule. It holds no land but its isle: by the Charter of the Tower it is part of Aldermere and owes the crown battle-mages in war, yet it keeps its own law, its own treasury and its own counsel. A few hundred sworn mages and their apprentices command more destructive power than any army on the Great Isle. Since the Black Dawn it has refused to tell the king what it knows of the Binding of the Blackspire.
Character: Brilliant, aloof and secretive. The Conclave believes magic must stay in the hands of the few who can be trusted with it, which in its view means itself. It serves the crown when the crown asks politely and pays well, bargains with every power for knowledge, and treats kings as passing weather. Its mages speak in careful half-truths and never forget a slight to the Tower.
Economy: Fees for spells, wards and scrying from every court that can pay, the crown's stipend under the Charter, enchanted goods, and centuries of hoarded wealth. It grows nothing and buys its food in Aldermere. Coin: Aldermere's silver crowns, held in the Tower's own treasury. Output about 300 crowns a head a year, 2.7 million crowns in all; farming 0%, crafts and mining 30%, trade and services 70%. Debt 0% of a year's output, budget +5% (surplus), growth 1% a year, prices rising 2% a year, 0% of hands idle. It grows 20% of the food and 60% of the wood and charcoal it needs.

author: mik
simulationRules:
IN SHORT: A medieval fantasy world in the year 523, with no gunpowder or modern technology; news travels by courier, ship and sending-spell. Magic is real and powerful, but in few hands: ordinary people have no access to it, while rulers and powers with the means hire wizards, witches and priests whose spells can change a battle - fire and storms rained on an army, walls cracked, fleets becalmed, wards raised, enemies scried. Such magic is costly, its users are few and can be killed, bought or turned, and a wizard's spell answers a government's order like any other force. The Iron Horde's overlord Malgrath is a necromancer of terrible power; Morrowgast's Hag-Queens work blood-witchcraft that has changed their people; the Order of the Lantern's knights wield a blessed light against both.
Peoples: humans in five kingdoms of the Great Isle and in Morrowgast, Veyl, the Salt Isles, the Lantern and the Lakeshore clans; orcs of the Northern Isle (the Iron Horde) and the north-western islet (the Ashen Exiles); dwarves in the Deepholds of the Eastern Isle; elves in the Elderwood.
The five human kingdoms are mostly at peace with each other, bound by marriages and old treaties, though border feuds and succession quarrels flare into short wars every few years. The great threats are the Iron Horde across the northern strait and Morrowgast on the south-eastern arm of the Great Isle.
The Conclave of the Lake is a landless order of wizards inside Aldermere: a client of the crown that supplies its battle-mages by charter, but an actor of its own with its own diplomacy, ambitions and secrets.
Years are counted from the crowning of Aldric the Founder, first King of Aldermere (year 1); earlier years are counted backwards (negative).
[ECONOMY] Every realm's wealth is reckoned in Aldermere silver crowns, so that realms compare: a labourer earns about a crown a week, and a realm's output a head a year runs from about 10 crowns (the exiles) to 300 (the Conclave). Each polity's note gives its coin, its value in crowns and its economy.
[WAR AND CONQUEST] Wars here are told, not calculated. A polity with a reason to conquer may contest regions of an enemy that border its land or that its ships can reach; who wins is judged from the two sides' strength of arms, their magic, the ground, the season, supply, allies and chance, and the winner takes the region. Conquered land becomes the conqueror's by law only by treaty, the loser's fall, or a season held unchallenged. A week of war takes one to three regions at most for a whole army.

startingTimelineText:
It is the first day of the year 523 of the Crown, and winter lies over the known world. North is the top of the map. The known world is five lands in a cold ocean:

THE GREAT ISLE, by far the largest, runs in a long arc from the west across the south of the world to a far south-eastern arm.
- Westmarch holds its south-western lowlands and harbours (capital Bellhaven), facing the Thornshaw, Pelcrest, Eldholt and Embermarsh seas.
- Aldermere holds the heart of the Isle around Lake Halmoor (capital Aldermere, on the lake shore). It borders Westmarch to the west, Hollowcrown to the north and Sunvale to the east; its south coast faces the Ostcombe Sea.
- Hollowcrown holds the central mountains and foothills north of Aldermere (capital Hollowcrown, in the Crownlands), between Aldermere and Thornwatch.
- Thornwatch holds the northern coast (capital Thornwatch Keep, in the Wardenmark), facing the Northern Isle across the narrow strait of Fenmark Bay and the Ravenheath Sea.
- The Order of the Lantern holds one mountain fastness, Lanternhold, in the peaks east of Hollowcrown.
- Sunvale holds the warm southern lowlands east of Aldermere (capital Solenne, on the Sunvale Riviera), its coasts on the Ostcombe Sea, Lorford Bay and the Belford Sea.
- East of Sunvale lie the Ashlands, unruled hills and coasts, and beyond them, at the far south-eastern end of the Isle, the Coven-Realm of Morrowgast (capital Morrowgast, in the Coven Hollow), ringed by Belbarrow, Redmoor, Yrreach and Saltholt bays and the Belford Sea.
- Much of the Isle outside the realms is unruled: the high peaks around Aldermere and Hollowcrown, the Ashlands, the wild coasts.

THE NORTHERN ISLE lies north of the Great Isle, a day's sail across the strait from Thornwatch. The Iron Horde's clans hold its south and centre, with the Blackspire in its peaks; its north and most of its coasts are wild land no one rules.

THE NORTH-WESTERN ISLET, in the frozen sea beyond the Northern Isle, is the Ashen Exiles' (Grukk's Landing), ringed by Harmere Bay and the Ulbarrow and Fencombe seas.

THE EASTERN ISLE lies far to the north-east, weeks of sailing from the Great Isle: Veyl on its north-western bay by the Irondale Sea, the Deepholds in the mountains east of Veyl, the Elderwood's forests in its south by the Ironcombe Sea. Most of it is wild.

THE SALT ISLES, small islands in the Ostcombe Sea south of Aldermere, between Westmarch and Sunvale, are the Brotherhood's (Red Harbour). Every ship between Westmarch, Aldermere and Sunvale passes within their reach.

An army crosses a realm in weeks; a ship crosses the Ostcombe Sea in days. When an event happens somewhere, name the realm, the region and the sea, and keep to this geography.

prehistory.summary: Over three thousand years of history: the elves' Elder Age, the humans' Landfall, Malgrath's first war and his binding, the rise of the five kingdoms of the Great Isle and Morrowgast's Blessing, to the Black Dawn of 520, when the Binding broke.

events.title: The First Heartwood
events.description: On the Eastern Isle the elves sang the first Heartwood out of the forest floor, a tree whose roots drink from the deep places of the world. Around it grew Caras Ithrael, oldest of all cities, and the Elder Age began.

events.title: The Pact of Root and Stone
events.description: Dwarves who had delved the eastern peaks met the elves at the forest's edge and swore the Pact of Root and Stone: dwarven iron for elven timber and healing, and neither people would ever take up arms against the other. Karak Dûm, the first of the Deepholds, was hollowed out in the same century.

events.title: The Landfall
events.description: Ships of a people the elves had never seen came out of the western ocean and grounded on the southern shores of the Great Isle: humans, fleeing a homeland they called the Drowned West and would never speak of plainly. Within three generations their villages lined every southern river.

events.title: First Blood on the Strait
events.description: Human fishermen crossing the northern strait met the orc clans of the Northern Isle, who had lived there since before the elves' songs began. The meeting ended in slaughter on both sides, and the raids across the strait that followed have never fully stopped.

events.title: The Thirteen Apprentices
events.description: Against the counsel of many, the elves of Caras Ithrael took thirteen gifted humans into the Heartwood and taught them the art of magic. Every human wizard, witch and spell-priest since has learned from someone who learned from one of the thirteen.

quote.text: We have given them fire. Let us hope we have also given them the wisdom to fear it.
quote.speaker: Ilmarë the Elder

events.title: The Banishment of Malgrath
events.description: Malgrath, the most brilliant of the thirteen, was caught in the roots of the Heartwood binding the dying to his will so that he would never die himself. The elves cast him out of the Eastern Isle. He sailed north with a handful of followers and was not seen for a generation.

events.title: The Raising of the Blackspire
events.description: In the northern peaks of the Northern Isle a black tower rose in a single winter night. Malgrath had completed his working: his heart stopped and he did not die. The orcs named him the Unbreathing, and one by one their clan chiefs came to the Blackspire to kneel or to be broken.

events.title: The First War of the Spire begins
events.description: The orc clans, bound into one horde under the Blackspire, crossed the strait in a thousand longships. They burned the young human settlements of the north coast and landed on the Eastern Isle, where the Elderwood burned for the first time in its history.

events.title: The Battle of the Weeping Fields
events.description: Elves, dwarves and the human chieftains of the Great Isle fought the Horde together for the first and only time, and broke it in a three-day battle in the north. Malgrath could not be killed, so the elves bound him: the elf-queen Saelind gave her life to weave a ward around the Blackspire that held him inside it.

quote.text: He cannot die, so he must wait. Let him wait a thousand years.
quote.speaker: Saelind

events.title: The Fading begins
events.description: After Saelind's death the Elderwood never recovered its numbers. Fewer elf children were born each century, and the elves withdrew from the affairs of the younger peoples, keeping watch over the Binding from afar.

events.title: The Vision of the Silver Flame
events.description: In a mountain hollow at the heart of the Great Isle the shepherd-prophetess Ysa saw a flame of silver burning on bare rock without fuel. She preached that it was the light of the one true god, and that all magic not kindled from it was theft. Her followers built the first shrine around the flame, which they say still burns.

events.title: The Beacon Line
events.description: The human chiefs of the north coast built a line of signal fires along the shore facing the Northern Isle, so that a raid seen at one end could be answered at the other. The watchers of the Beacon Line became the ancestors of Thornwatch.

events.title: The Charter of the Three Tables
events.description: Human, dwarf and elf traders on the Eastern Isle's great bay signed the Charter of the Three Tables and founded Veyl, a free city owing nothing to any crown. Its glassmakers soon learned to make lenses, mirrors and the famous crystal of Veyl, and its bankers to lend against them.

events.title: The Crowning of Aldric the Founder
events.description: On the shore of the great lake, Aldric of the lake tribes was crowned first King of Aldermere after uniting the river chiefs by marriage, oath and war. Ever since, the peoples of the Great Isle have counted the years from his crowning.

quote.text: Let every year be counted from this day, so that none forget who first brought law to this isle.
quote.speaker: Aldric the Founder

events.title: The Lake Road is finished
events.description: Aldermere completed the paved Lake Road from its lake capital to the harbours of the west, and placed toll-gates along it. The road made the western harbours rich, and the tolls would be quarrelled over for five centuries.

events.title: The Hollow Crown
events.description: The priests of the Silver Flame crowned their first priest-queen in the mountain hollow where Ysa had her vision. Her crown was a ring of silver with nothing at its centre but the flame's light, and the realm took its name from it: Hollowcrown.

events.title: The Charter of Bells
events.description: The merchant towns of the western lowlands bought their freedom from Aldermere for a sum in silver that emptied the royal treasury's rivals for a generation. They rang every bell from Bellhaven to Belldam and named their new realm Westmarch, ruled by a council of merchant princes.

events.title: The War of the Two Crowns
events.description: Aldermere's southern princes crowned their own king in Solenne. Five years of war ended in the Treaty of the Vines, by which Aldermere recognised the Kingdom of Sunvale and a royal marriage bound the two houses. They have married into each other ever since.

events.title: The First Warden
events.description: Aldermere and Hollowcrown jointly granted the north coast to Hadric Stonehand, captain of the Beacon Line, as a hereditary march, on condition that he and his heirs hold the strait against the Horde for all time. Thornwatch Keep was raised on the rock where the first beacon burned.

events.title: The Blight Years
events.description: A grey blight killed the crops of the Great Isle's south-eastern arm three years running. When the lords fled, the village wise-women fed the people with spells no priest would sanction, and in 304 thirteen of them swore the Covenant of the Coven and ruled in the lords' place. The land took the name of their meeting-place: Morrowgast.

events.title: The Seers' Warning
events.description: The seers of the Elderwood reported that the Binding of the Blackspire had begun to thin. The kingdoms of the Great Isle, busy with their own quarrels, did not answer the elves' envoys.

events.title: The Mutiny of the Salt Isles
events.description: Sailors of Westmarch's war fleet mutinied off the small southern islands, freed the orc galley-slaves chained at their oars and declared themselves the Brotherhood of the Salt Isles. They have raided the shipping of every crown since, and taken any crew that will sail under their flag.

events.title: The Red Sabbath
events.description: When a Sunvalese army marched into Morrowgast to end the Coven's rule, the Hag-Queens worked the first great blood-rite on their own militia. The men who rose from it were taller, fevered and fearless, and Sunvale's army did not come home. Morrowgast calls it the Blessing.

events.title: The Burning of the Beacons
events.description: The largest orc raid in three centuries crossed the strait and burned half the beacons of Thornwatch before the Warden's levies drove it back into the sea. The raiders sang the name of the Blackspire as they fought, though its master was still bound.

events.title: Sunvale's Second Crusade
events.description: Sunvale invaded Morrowgast again, this time with Hollowcrown's blessing and its priests. The Blessed of the Coven routed the crusaders in the fens, and the bodies of the priests were never returned.

events.title: The Lamp of Anselm
events.description: Anselm, a priest of the Silver Flame who had survived the crusade, carried a lantern lit from the flame into the mountains and founded a brotherhood of knights sworn to destroy the Coven and every unholy magic. Hollowcrown's priests called his teaching dangerous; the knights called themselves the Order of the Lantern and built Lanternhold.

quote.text: Light is not a thing you pray for. It is a thing you carry into the dark.
quote.speaker: Anselm the Lampbearer
quote.role: Founder of the Order of the Lantern

events.title: The War of the Lake Road
events.description: Aldermere doubled the tolls on the Lake Road and Westmarch closed its harbours to Aldermere's wool. Five years of skirmishes followed until the Concord of the Lake in 429 fixed the tolls by treaty and set out how the five kingdoms would settle their quarrels in council. Both sides still say the other cheats.

events.title: The Concord of the Lake
events.description: At Aldermere the five kingdoms of the Great Isle swore the Concord of the Lake: tolls on the Lake Road fixed for all time, quarrels between the kingdoms to be heard in council before swords are drawn, and the King of Aldermere to call the council. It has kept the peace, mostly, for ninety years.

events.title: The Fall of Karak Varn
events.description: Miners of Karak Varn, the deepest of the Deepholds, broke into a cavern of fire and something that lived in it. The hold was sealed with its last defenders inside. The dwarves do not speak of what they found, and their mines have not gone as deep since.

events.title: The Strait Compact
events.description: Hollowcrown and Thornwatch swore to defend each other against the Horde. Hollowcrown sends priests and silver to the wall; the Wardens send nothing south but warnings.

events.title: The Last Birth
events.description: The last elf child born in the Elderwood came into the world on the spring equinox. None has been born since, and the elves no longer speak of when the next will be.

events.title: The Glass Senate
events.description: Veyl replaced its old council of the Three Tables with an elected Glass Senate, open to any citizen who could pay its tax. Its first decree: that Veyl would lend to any power, and fight for none.

events.title: The Grey Cough
events.description: A coughing sickness came ashore in Westmarch's harbours and spread along the Lake Road. By the time it burned out, one in five of Aldermere's people was dead, and Westmarch was blamed for it in every Aldermere tavern.

events.title: The Crowning of Edric IV
events.description: Edric IV was crowned King of Aldermere at twenty-four, in a court still in mourning after the Grey Cough. He has ruled carefully, by precedent and council, ever since.

events.title: A Boy King in Solenne
events.description: Florian II was crowned King of Sunvale at nine years old. His ministers have governed in his name ever since, and he has shown little wish to take the reins from them.

events.title: The Night of Thirteen Candles
events.description: Six of the thirteen Hag-Queens of Morrowgast died on a single night. The remaining seven named Mother Vesk first among them, and under her the Blessing has been worked on more of Morrowgast's people than ever before.

events.title: The Oathbreaking
events.description: When the Blackspire's voice commanded the clans to give their young to its rites, the chief Grukk refused and broke his oath to the Spire before his whole clan. He led them across the sea to a frozen islet in the far north-west. The Horde has hunted the Oathbreakers ever since.

quote.text: I have eaten his bread and fought his wars. I will not feed him my children.
quote.speaker: Grukk Oathbreaker

events.title: Queen Ysolde is crowned
events.description: Ysolde, High Priestess of the Silver Flame, was crowned Queen of Hollowcrown under the hollow crown. She has made the realm sterner and more devout, and has quarrelled openly with Sunvale's court over its morals.

events.title: The Battle of the Grey Strand
events.description: The Warden of Thornwatch fell at the Grey Strand repelling an orc landing, and his son Garrick, called Stonehand, took up the wardenship on the beach where his father died. Thornwatch's appeal to the other kingdoms for money to rebuild the wall was heard in council and not paid.

events.title: The Marriage of the Lake and the Vines
events.description: Florian II of Sunvale married Princess Elowen of Aldermere, King Edric's niece, renewing the oldest friendship among the kingdoms.

events.title: Cassia Venn elected First Magistrate
events.description: The Glass Senate of Veyl elected Cassia Venn, a banker's daughter who had financed half the kingdoms' debts, as First Magistrate.

events.title: Red Mara takes the Brotherhood
events.description: The quartermaster Red Mara killed the old Captain-General in a duel on the quay at Red Harbour and was acclaimed by every crew. Under her the Brotherhood's raids on Westmarch shipping have grown bolder.

events.title: Durgrim Ashbeard becomes Thane-King
events.description: Durgrim Ashbeard was raised to the stone throne of Karak Dûm. He doubled the price of dwarven steel and sells it to every buyer.

events.title: The Black Dawn
events.description: At midwinter the Blackspire was seen to shine with a black light from Thornwatch's walls, two hundred miles away. In Caras Ithrael the Lady Ithrael woke weeping: the Binding has broken. For the first time in more than fifteen hundred years Malgrath speaks to his chiefs in his own voice, and the clans are gathering under the Spire.

quote.text: The ward is gone. What Saelind bought with her life, we have spent.
quote.speaker: The Lady Ithrael

events.title: The Lakeshore Fens are taken
events.description: Aldermere's knights occupied the last fenland of the Free Clans of the Lakeshore, at Marlford Vale, to secure the lake against a feared invasion. The clans were scattered into the reeds and the hills, and their moot under Wenna of the Reeds has sworn to win their land back.

events.title: Longships off Thornwatch
events.description: Iron Horde longships were sighted off Thornwatch's coast in numbers not seen since the Burning of the Beacons. Barhythe was raided and burned. Garrick Stonehand has called every man of the march to the wall.

events.title: Blessed raiders in the Ashlands
events.description: War-bands of Morrowgast's Blessed crossed the unclaimed lands between the Coven-Realm and Sunvale and burned three Sunvalese villages on its eastern border. Sunvale's ministers protested, and paid the Brotherhood to patrol the coast instead of sending soldiers.

events.title: The Veyl Ledgers
events.description: A clerk who fled Veyl sold Aldermere a copy of the Glass Senate's ledgers, which appear to show Veyl's bankers lending gold against the iron of the Northern Isle. Veyl calls the ledgers forgeries. Nobody believes either side.

events.title: The Lantern's Vow
events.description: Grand Master Aldous Cray vowed before the Order that the Lantern would march against Morrowgast within the year, and asked every kingdom of the Great Isle for men and silver. Queen Ysolde has not answered.

events.title: An envoy from the Oathbreakers
events.description: An orc envoy of the Ashen Exiles came under a white branch to Thornwatch Keep, offering the secrets of the Blackspire's defences in exchange for land on the Great Isle. Garrick Stonehand has kept the envoy, and the offer, to himself.

events.title: King Edric calls the Council
events.description: Invoking the Concord of the Lake for the first time in a generation, King Edric IV summoned the rulers of the five kingdoms to a Council of the Kingdoms at Aldermere in the spring of 523, to answer the Black Dawn and the threat from the south-east.

quote.text: We have quarrelled over tolls for a hundred years. I would rather not quarrel over them in the Horde's slave pens.
quote.speaker: Edric IV

events.title: The Tower on Wyn
events.description: Aldwen, one of the Thirteen Apprentices, came home to the lake tribes and raised a tower of white stone on the isle of Wyn in the great lake. She took human students of her own there, the first school of magic outside the Elderwood.

events.title: The Oath of the Few
events.description: Aldwen's students had fought at the Weeping Fields and seen what Malgrath, one of their own, had become. They swore the Oath of the Few: magic would be taught only to those the Tower could watch for the rest of their lives. The Conclave has kept magic from the common people ever since.

quote.text: One of thirteen became Malgrath. We will not teach a thousand and hope for better.
quote.speaker: Aldwen of Wyn

events.title: The Charter of the Tower
events.description: King Aldric II of Aldermere and the Conclave signed the Charter of the Tower. The isle of Wyn and its mages were made part of the kingdom, but under their own law; in return the Conclave owes the crown battle-mages whenever Aldermere goes to war.

events.title: Fire on the Lake Road
events.description: In the War of the Lake Road, three of the Conclave's battle-mages burned Westmarch's barges and the toll-forts they had seized in a single night. Westmarch sued for peace within the year, and has never forgiven the Tower.

events.title: The Silence of the Tower
events.description: Summoned by King Edric IV after the Black Dawn, Archmagister Corvane Thule refused to tell the king what the Conclave knows of the Binding of the Blackspire. Rumours spread in Aldermere's court that some in the Tower have been studying Malgrath's art.

canonicalUpdates.summary: Bound by the Concord of the Lake, but still quarrelling over the Lake Road's tolls and blaming each other for the Grey Cough.
The oldest friendship among the kingdoms, renewed by Florian II's marriage to King Edric's niece.
Respectful partners in the Concord; Aldermere finds Hollowcrown's piety tiresome.
Aldermere relies on Thornwatch's wall but has never paid what the Wardens ask for it.
Allies under the Strait Compact; Hollowcrown's priests and silver help hold the wall.
Queen Ysolde despises Sunvale's court and its morals; Sunvale finds Hollowcrown grim and preachy.
Trading partners whose merchants and ministers understand each other well.
Hollowcrown's priests call the Lantern's teaching dangerous, but cannot deny its courage.

canonicalUpdates.b: The Free Clans of the Lakeshore
canonicalUpdates.summary: Aldermere's knights took the clans' last fens; the clans have sworn to win them back.
The wall and the Horde have been at war in all but name for a thousand years.
Aldermere fears the Horde's return above everything else.
The elves bound Malgrath once, at terrible cost, and he has not forgotten.
The Horde hunts the Oathbreakers wherever they go.
The Exiles have offered Thornwatch the Spire's secrets; the Warden has not decided whether to trust them.
Morrowgast's Blessed raid Sunvale's eastern villages; Sunvale has twice failed to conquer the Coven.
The Order of the Lantern exists to destroy the Coven, and has vowed to march this year.
The Silver Flame calls the Coven's blood-witchcraft an abomination.
Veyl buys dwarven steel and lends against it; the trade has made both rich.
Old friends under the Pact of Root and Stone, though the dwarves find the elves' gloom wearing.
Aldermere believes Veyl has lent gold to the Horde.

canonicalUpdates.a: The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles
canonicalUpdates.summary: The Brotherhood raids Westmarch's shipping, and Westmarch hangs every pirate it catches.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Concord of the Lake
canonicalUpdates.terms: The Lake Road's tolls are fixed; quarrels between the five kingdoms are heard in council, called by the King of Aldermere, before swords are drawn.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Strait Compact
canonicalUpdates.terms: Hollowcrown and Thornwatch defend each other against the Horde; Hollowcrown sends priests and silver to the wall.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Marriage of the Lake and the Vines
canonicalUpdates.terms: The royal houses of Aldermere and Sunvale are joined by marriage and consult each other on matters of war.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Pact of Root and Stone
canonicalUpdates.terms: Sworn in the Elder Age: dwarven iron for elven timber and healing, and neither people will ever take up arms against the other.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Steel Notes of Veyl
canonicalUpdates.terms: Veyl buys the Deepholds' steel and sells it on across the world, lending against future deliveries.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Return of the Unbreathing
canonicalUpdates.state: The Binding of the Blackspire has broken. Malgrath is gathering the orc clans under the Spire and testing Thornwatch's wall; the elves fear a second War of the Spire.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Spreading Blessing
canonicalUpdates.state: Under Mother Vesk the Blessing is worked on more of Morrowgast's people every year, and its war-bands raid ever deeper into Sunvale's eastern lands. The Order of the Lantern has vowed to march.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Council of the Kingdoms
canonicalUpdates.state: King Edric IV has called the five kingdoms to council at Aldermere in the spring of 523 to answer the Black Dawn and Morrowgast. Old quarrels over the Lake Road, the wall's cost and Sunvale's morals stand in the way.

canonicalUpdates.title: The Hunt for the Oathbreakers
canonicalUpdates.state: The Horde's longships hunt the Ashen Exiles' islet, and Grukk Oathbreaker looks for an ally among the humans.

canonicalUpdates.summary: Bound by the Charter of the Tower, but the Archmagister's silence about the Binding has soured the king's trust.
The Silver Flame teaches that all magic not kindled from it is theft; the Conclave thinks Hollowcrown's priests are superstitious.

Aldermere.government: Feudal monarchy bound by the Concord of the Lake

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: the silver crown (the reckoning coin of the Great Isle))

Westmarch.government: Merchant oligarchy under the Charter of Bells
Westmarch.leader: Marro Bellweather, First Prince of Westmarch

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: the gilder (1 gilder = 1.2 crowns))

Hollowcrown.government: Theocratic monarchy of the Silver Flame
Hollowcrown.leader: Ysolde, Queen and High Priestess of the Silver Flame

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: the hallowed mark, struck from its own mountain silver (1 mark = 1.5 crowns))
Silver crowns (its own coin: Aldermere's crowns, and the Warden's iron ward-notes, promises to pay after the war (1 ward-note = 0.6 crowns))

Sunvale.government: Court monarchy ruled by its ministers

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: the golden sol (1 sol = 3 crowns))

The Iron Horde of Gor-Vathra.leader: Malgrath the Unbreathing, Master of the Blackspire

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: no coin of its own: tribute in iron bars, captives and plunder, reckoned in iron weights (1 weight = 0.5 crowns), and Veyl's gold for its iron)

The Coven-Realm of Morrowgast.leader: Mother Vesk, First of the Hag-Queens

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: the coven groat, base silver stamped with a crow (1 groat = 0.4 crowns))

The Glass Republic of Veyl.leader: Cassia Venn, First Magistrate of Veyl

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: the glass ducat, the most trusted coin in the world (1 ducat = 5 crowns))

The Deepholds of Karak Dûm.capital: Karak Dûm, in The Halls of Karak Dûm
The Deepholds of Karak Dûm.leader: Durgrim Ashbeard, Thane-King of Karak Dûm

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: the anvil, a heavy gold coin (1 anvil = 10 crowns))

The Elderwood.leader: The Lady Ithrael, Lady of the Elderwood

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: no coin: gifts and barter among the elves; others reckon its trade in crowns)

The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles.capital: Red Harbour, in Red Harbour Cay
The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles.government: Pirate brotherhood ruled by its captains
The Brotherhood of the Salt Isles.leader: Red Mara, Captain-General of the Brotherhood

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: whatever it takes: mixed coin reckoned in 'pieces' (1 piece = 1 crown))

The Order of the Lantern.leader: Aldous Cray, Grand Master of the Order of the Lantern

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: Hollowcrown's hallowed marks and alms in every coin of the Great Isle)

The Free Clans of the Lakeshore.capital: None: its clan-mothers hold their moot wherever the clans are camped
The Free Clans of the Lakeshore.leader: Wenna of the Reeds, First of the Clan-Mothers

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: no coin of its own: barter in fish, fowl, reeds and furs)

The Ashen Exiles.leader: Grukk Oathbreaker, Chief of the Ashen Exiles

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: no coin: barter, and Horde iron taken in the flight)

The Conclave of the Lake.capital: The Tower of Stars, on the isle of Wyn in Aldermere's lake
The Conclave of the Lake.government: Magocracy of sworn mages under the Charter of the Tower
The Conclave of the Lake.leader: Corvane Thule, Archmagister of the Conclave

economy.currency: Silver crowns (its own coin: Aldermere's silver crowns, held in the Tower's own treasury)
